findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record an audit of tests that read or reset the bound: grep tests/ for `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` and `reload(` / `sys.modules` manipulation of `_ref_lock`, and list each hit with its disposition.
evidence: Approach: 'every in-process caller sees it' and 'The fail-closed contract stays proven by ... test_timeout_raises_reflocktimeout'
Testing names only five modules; 'The class' says 35 test files drive the ref-lock backend.
findings.finding: The plan raises the bound for every test in the session. It does not say anyone audited tests that may depend on the production 5.0 value. Examples: a test that asserts the value, passes a timeout derived from it, reloads `_ref_lock` (which would silently reset the bound to 5.0), or relies on a real git call actually timing out near 5 s. Such a test would now wait up to 60 s or assert the wrong value. Only make verify would catch it, late. The plan names test_ref_lock_blob_read_budget as one such dependent but treats the rest of the 35 files as safe without a stated check.
scenarios: A test spawns a genuinely hung git and expects HELD within roughly 5 s. It now blocks for 60 s and may trip a pytest-timeout.
A test calls importlib.reload on _ref_lock. The bound reverts to 5.0 for the rest of that worker, and the class silently reopens.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Testing: '`grep -rn "_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS\|reload(.*_ref_lock" tests/` — every hit is either a monkeypatch (restores to the session value) or listed here with why it is unaffected.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the shim delay only the cleanup `update-ref -d refs/reconciler/gate`, reproduce the reported failure (the delete times out and the pause is not cleared) on the pre-fix tree, and have the new test assert the pause is cleared under that delay.
evidence: "delay 5.6 s: both parameters fail. `[doctor]` raises ... from `set_pause`, re-raised as `RepairPauseError: Error: doctor repair could not acquire its reconciliation pause`"
"In the reported run the slow call was the cleanup delete of the same ref, which takes the same path."
"a PATH `git` shim that sleeps 5.6 s before `update-ref`"
findings.finding: The reproduction and the new regression test delay EVERY `update-ref`, so the failure surfaces at `set_pause` ('could not acquire its reconciliation pause'). The reported failure was the cleanup delete timing out. The plan asserts that the delete 'takes the same path' but never reproduces a slow cleanup-only delete, so the original symptom (owned pause not cleared) is neither reproduced nor regression-tested. Delaying every update-ref by 5.6 s also adds several 5.6 s stalls to every `make verify` run.
scenarios: A future change makes the cleanup delete use a different timeout or exception path. The new test still passes because it trips at `set_pause` first, yet the reported 'pause left behind' failure recurs.
Each `make verify` pays roughly 5.6 s × (number of update-ref calls in the doctor in-flight path) of pure sleep.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the shim match `update-ref -d` (or `update-ref` with the delete argument) for `refs/reconciler/gate` and sleep only on that call. Pass all other git calls straight through. Record the pre-fix failure (pause left behind / RefLockTimeoutError on the delete) and the post-fix pass. Optionally keep the existing all-calls 5.6 s repro as narrative evidence only.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the new shim test behaves on Windows: reuse the shim and skip guard from `test_advisory_lock.py`'s existing slow-git test, or mark it POSIX-only with an explicit skip reason.
evidence: "with a PATH `git` shim that sleeps 5.6 s before `update-ref` and records each delayed call to a file ... assert ... that the shim recorded at least one delayed `update-ref`"
Windows process creation does not execute extensionless scripts found on PATH; the PATHEXT lookup picks up `git.exe`.
findings.finding: The new test relies on a PATH `git` shim. On Windows, `subprocess` resolves `git` through CreateProcess/PATHEXT to `git.exe`, so an extensionless shell-script shim is never executed. The real git runs undelayed, and the test's own required assertion ('the shim recorded at least one delayed `update-ref`') fails. The plan names no platform guard or Windows-compatible shim.
findings.location: Testing — 'with a PATH `git` shim that sleeps 5.6 s before `update-ref` and records each delayed call to a file'
scenarios: Windows developer workstation or Windows CI runner running `make verify`: the new test fails on its 'shim recorded a delayed update-ref' assertion even though the fix is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the existing slow-git shim helper/pattern from test_advisory_lock.py, including whatever platform guard it already has. If it has none, add `pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == 'win32', reason='PATH shell shim')`.

findings.finding: The planned `test_a_slow_local_git_call_does_not_fail_the_repair_pause` rebuilds a PATH `git` shim that sleeps 5.6 s before `update-ref`. An identical shim already exists in `test_advisory_lock.py::test_ref_backend_roundtrip_survives_a_slow_local_git_call`, which already proves the same guarantee (a slow local update-ref under the session bound does not produce a false HELD) once the plan removes that module's override. The new test adds a second sleep-based check of the same session-level setting, and each delayed update-ref on the doctor path (set_pause, clear, cleanup) adds about 5.6 s of wall time to `make verify`.

scenarios: make verify on a loaded host gets a second multi-update-ref test that sleeps 5.6 s per call, for coverage the advisory-lock slow test already gives
